body.statement:
For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\),
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)
 =\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.
\]
Static equality is decidable using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons with adjacency matrices and canonical block bitsets. The primary procedure takes \(O(p^3)\) Meek-closure initialization, enumerates every consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\) exactly once with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay, and applies the output-linear canonical partition lift \(\mathsf L_C\). Moreover \(|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!\), sharply, with equality for the complete-skeleton all-singleton state. If shortest legal-reversal certificates are requested, the constructive covered-reversal scan uses \(O(p^5)\) time per emitted state and returns for each \(D\) a path of length \(\delta(C,D)\). Exact state memoization is required only by the legal-reversal breadth-first fallback, which is complete and also returns shortest certificates.
body.justification: The population characterization is operational because the canonical background PDAG and unique partition lift yield exact-once enumeration with explicit delay, sharp size, and shortest-certificate guarantees.
body.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 handles PDAG extensions but not target partitions; the canonical-lift bijection proves output-linear lifting, path independence, and legality of the constructive shortest certificates.
body.consumer: Component enumeration supplies every graph-specific adjustment and path functional needed for possible-effect analysis, with complete state labels and optional shortest legal-reversal certificates.
body.proof_tex:
The bijection in \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\), applied to the constructions in \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), \(\texttt{def:canonical-partition-lift}\), and \(\texttt{def:component-enumerator}\), proves that the primary procedure emits every state of \(\mathcal R(C)\) exactly once. The same proposition and \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)
 =\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.
\]

For the static decision bound, skeleton equality costs \(O(p^2)\) adjacency comparisons. Enumerating labelled triples and checking the two incoming adjacencies and the absent shielding adjacency costs \(O(p^3)\). Encode each parent block by a canonical \(p\)-bit incidence vector. The blocks are disjoint and their total number is \(O(p^2)\), so forming and comparing all vertex-indexed nonsingleton families uses \(O(p^3)\) elementary bit comparisons. A final scan of the \(O(p^2)\) adjacencies compares \(F(C)\) and \(F(D)\). Thus \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\) is decidable in \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons.

After \(O(p^3)\) Meek-closure initialization, \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\) emits each consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\) exactly once with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay. The canonical-lift proposition proves that forming \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) is output-linear and introduces neither a transport choice nor a duplicate. It also proves
\[
 |\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!,
\]
and proves sharpness: for the complete skeleton with all parent blocks singleton, acyclic orientations are in bijection with the \(p!\) total orders, all have no unshielded collider, and all lie in one component.

When certificates are requested, the constructive monotone covered-edge path supplied in \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\) retains all background arrows, canonically lifts every intermediate graph, and therefore consists of legal reversals. Its safe running-time bound is \(O(p^5)\) per output, and \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) identifies its length as \(\delta(C,D)\), hence as shortest possible. In the fallback only, breadth-first search explores the finite legal-move graph and uses an exact visited-state set; it therefore emits no duplicate, terminates after at most \(p!\) states, and its predecessor tree gives shortest paths.
